content.subject: Trump Orders Contractors to Alert White House on Congress
content.preview_text: Trump touts Asia deals, stocks enter a correction and Denmark accuses Russia of a murder plot.

stories.title: Trump Orders Contractors to Alert the White House Before Talking to Congress

photo.alt: The U.S. Capitol dome behind bare trees; file photo.

paragraphs: President Trump on Friday ordered federal contractors to alert the White House before sharing information with Congress. CNBC reports the order also tells them to withhold material the administration deems confidential. It applies to contractors and their subcontractors.

Companies that fail to comply could lose existing contracts or be suspended from future federal work, the order said. CNBC reports the restrictions could face legal challenges. That is most likely if contractors are told to withhold subpoenaed information.

The move comes as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January. Rep. Jamie Raskin, the incoming House Judiciary chairman, is focusing on officials using the Signal app, NBC News reports. He said there is significant evidence records were destroyed.

Why it matters. Al Jazeera reports Raskin asked agencies including the FBI and ICE to recover such records by December 3. The administration has signaled it intends to fight Democratic probes. The clash over oversight could end up in court.

stories.title: Trump Touts Asia Trade Deals at a Nearly Two-Hour Press Conference

photo.alt: Four handheld microphones on a dark cloth; file photo.

paragraphs: President Trump held a White House press conference on Friday after returning from Asia. CBS News reports he called it one of the most successful presidential visits to Asia in American history. He spoke for nearly two hours.

Trump said he met more than 20 world leaders and secured two new trade deals, CBS reported. He said about 10 others are coming very soon. He also said he wants to heavily tax U.S. companies that build data centers overseas.

Trump said he discussed former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. CNBC reports Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said earlier that Huang did not come up in his own talks. Trump said he would like to see Huang restored as CEO.

Why it matters. Trump downplayed recent tech outages across several industries as all separate events, CBS News reports. He also said he has not lost confidence in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. CBS News reports some Republicans in Congress have called for Lutnick to testify.

stories.title: Stocks Fall Into a Correction as Bitcoin Hits a Two-Year Low

photo.alt: A phone screen showing red stock charts; file photo.

paragraphs: The S&P 500 and the Dow closed in correction territory on Friday. CNBC reports both are now more than 10% below their records. The Nasdaq Composite erased its gain for 2026.

Nvidia led the slide. CNBC reports Nvidia shares fell 14% on Friday for a seventh straight weekly drop. The stock is down 46% over that stretch. Investors are worried about the company after the departure of Jensen Huang.

Crypto fell too. Reuters reports bitcoin fell 5.10% to $55,830 by 11:13 p.m. ET on Friday. That was its lowest level since September 2024. Earlier Friday it dropped below $60,000 for the first time since July.

Why it matters. Reuters reports worries about AI spending and rising borrowing costs have weighed on risky assets. CNBC cites the Anthropic IPO and a Federal Reserve losing the inflation fight. U.S. markets are closed for the weekend.

stories.title: Trump Says Putin Wants a Deal but Holds Off on Ukraine Guarantees

photo.alt: A damaged apartment building in Odesa, Ukraine; file photo.

paragraphs: President Trump said on Friday that he and Vladimir Putin held very good talks on Ukraine in China. Reuters reports Trump said there is a real good chance that we can get it done. He called Putin a friend.

Trump set aside the question of security guarantees for Ukraine, Reuters reported. He said a deal must come first. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said any quasi membership for Kyiv in NATO was unacceptable, according to Russian state media.

ABC News reports Trump said Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy are two guys that do not know how to end it. Trump said the two leaders have tremendous hatred. ABC notes Russia has continued to launch deadly attacks.

Why it matters. Trump called the gap between the two sides part of a public relations war. He said Putin would like to get this settled. Security guarantees have long been a sticking point in the talks, Reuters reported.

deep_dive.title: Why Denmark Is Expelling a Russian Diplomat

photo.alt: Bicycles parked outside row houses in Copenhagen; file photo.

paragraphs: Denmark said it will expel Russia's defense attache. The Guardian reports Danish officials suspect Moscow was behind a plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner. Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said the attache must leave within seven days. Police said they stopped the plot before a planned concert in September. The September 25 concert was later cancelled, officials said. Kyivstoner's real name is Albert Viktorovich Vasiliev, and he holds US and Ukrainian nationality, the Guardian reported.

Denmark's intelligence chief said it was his clear assessment that Russian intelligence services planned the attempt. NBC News reports two alleged gang members were arrested in connection with it. BBC News reports two people were charged with attempted murder and pleaded not guilty. Danish broadcaster DR, citing a court hearing, reported the men are suspected of being recruited for the killing, NBC News reported.

The Russian embassy called the allegations unsubstantiated, the BBC reported. It said Copenhagen had provided no evidence of Moscow's involvement. The embassy accused Denmark of provocations meant to frighten the Danish public. Russian state media cite Moscow's foreign ministry as saying it will respond to the expulsion.

Rasmussen said Denmark is working at the European level to tighten access for Russian nationals. He said Denmark is pushing toward a halt to all non-essential visas. He said the strongest response is to keep supporting Ukraine. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Saturday called the plot an attack on EU soil, BBC News reports.

03 / Deep dive

One story, explained.

Why Denmark Is Expelling a Russian Diplomat

What happened

Denmark said it will expel Russia's defense attache. The Guardian reports Danish officials suspect Moscow was behind a plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner. Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said the attache must leave within seven days. Police said they stopped the plot before a planned concert in September. The September 25 concert was later cancelled, officials said. Kyivstoner's real name is Albert Viktorovich Vasiliev, and he holds US and Ukrainian nationality, the Guardian reported.

Why it matters

Denmark's intelligence chief said it was his clear assessment that Russian intelligence services planned the attempt. NBC News reports two alleged gang members were arrested in connection with it. BBC News reports two people were charged with attempted murder and pleaded not guilty. Danish broadcaster DR, citing a court hearing, reported the men are suspected of being recruited for the killing, NBC News reported.

What each side says

The Russian embassy called the allegations unsubstantiated, the BBC reported. It said Copenhagen had provided no evidence of Moscow's involvement. The embassy accused Denmark of provocations meant to frighten the Danish public. Russian state media cite Moscow's foreign ministry as saying it will respond to the expulsion.

What comes next

Rasmussen said Denmark is working at the European level to tighten access for Russian nationals. He said Denmark is pushing toward a halt to all non-essential visas. He said the strongest response is to keep supporting Ukraine. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Saturday called the plot an attack on EU soil, BBC News reports.
